text:
Maya Chen: Quick idea: add a new runtime flag `latency_first` to prefer the lowest-latency serving pool for p99-sensitive routes. Thinking out loud about safety and observability.

Samir Patel: +1 for the feature but default it to off. if we steer too many requests we could blow through a pool quota and cascade. gradual launch only.

Priya Gupta: Agree on gradual. we need three safety layers: percent-based ramp, telemetry gate (compare p99 delta to baseline), and an automatic spillover when a pool nears capacity.

Ken Ito: Prototype config shape suggestion:

```
{
  "flag": "latency_first",
  "mode": "percent_ramp",
  "initial_percent": 3,
  "ramp_steps": [10,30,100],
  "eval_window_secs": 180,
  "baseline_window_secs": 3600,
  "gate_metric": "relative_p99_ms",
  "gate_threshold": 0.2,
  "spill_policy": "spill_to_least_loaded",
  "dry_run": true
}
```

Maya Chen: couple questions: (1) gate_threshold is relative (0.2 = 20% worse than baseline)? (2) how do we avoid oscillation when pools bounce between near-threshold?

Samir Patel: Yes relative is safer. For oscillation add hysteresis: require two consecutive violation windows before auto-revert and a cooldown period post-rollback.

Priya Gupta: Telemetry specifics: eval_window 2-5m, baseline 1h like above. Also add a small sample of decision audit events rather than full write flood. but critical aborts must be immediate and un-sampled.

deploy-bot: deploy started latency-first-canary v0.1 -> 4 hosts in us-west-2 (dry_run=true)

Ken Ito: Implementation note: runtime API should offer an endpoint `POST /runtime/flags/evaluate` which returns an object describing "would_route_to" vs "did_route_to" for dry runs so console can visualize impact without changing live routing. We should also add `GET /runtime/flags/decision-history?flag=latency_first&limit=50`.

Maya Chen: Console UX: show current gate metric (relative p99), last eval timestamp, users who initiated rollout, and a big red "abort rollout" button that sets a global fail-closed. Also highlight spill destinations and quota headroom.

Priya Gupta: Add gating acceptance tests: telemetry simulator that injects small latency regressions and a chaos test that simulates pool quota exhaustion. validate auto-spill and auto-revert behavior.

Samir Patel: Ops note: audit writes can be noisy. batching or probabilistic sampling is fine for ordinary decisions. we must however log every manual abort and every auto-revert synchronously to the audit store.

Maya Chen: Draft playbook idea: default off; run dry_run for 24h; ramp percents 3->10->30->100 with a gating pass at each step; require 2 consecutive ok evals to move forward; automatic revert on either gate breach or spill->other not meeting latency SLO. i'll spin up an RFC and link it here. https://redwood.internal/rfcs/latency-first-routing

Ken Ito: i'll mock the evaluate API in staging + add a small dashboard tile in console staging that shows "would vs did" routing heatmap. tagging @Priya to coordinate telemetry hooks.

Priya Gupta: On the telemetry side i'll add a streaming metric that computes relative_p99_ms per-route and a tiny alert rule that triggers an automated dry revert if we see >50% increase in errors.

Maya Chen: sounds good. if no objections i'll start the canary tomorrow morning and post the RFC link. :thumbsup:
